key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving and preserving their optoelectronic uniformity, decoupling morphology from electronic quality.
engineering_relevance: Perovskite solar-cell interfaces should be optimized for recombination suppression and electronic stability rather than surface smoothness alone.
method: Form mixed-dimensional heterostructures using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium-derived Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers.
Compare statistical AFM topography with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting.
Evaluate pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, with homogeneity largely preserved during aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not report device-level efficiency, quantitative aging conditions, or scalability, so photovoltaic deployment benefits remain to be established.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
